confirmed.title: Table vertical-align walk admits an inheritance that Chromium's UA sheet does not perform, and its unit premise cannot fail
confirmed.evidence: tests/setupStyles.ts:622-632: `// HTML Rendering's table UA rules inherit vertical-align only along table internals.` / `if (property === 'vertical-align' && element.matches('thead, tbody, tfoot, tr, th, td')) {` walks every `table, thead, tbody, tfoot, tr, th, td` ancestor and returns 'inherited' if any of them departed, breaking only at `table`. Chromium 141.0.7390.37 html.css (fetched at that tag): `thead`, `tbody`, and `tfoot` each have `vertical-align: middle` (lines 270-286), `table > tr { vertical-align: middle; }` (289-291), and only `tr` and `td, th` have `vertical-align: inherit` (301-310). A headless probe on HeadlessChrome/141.0.7390.37 read `<table><tbody><tr><td>`: td = `middle` with no sheet, td = `middle` with `table { vertical-align: middle }`, and td = `middle` with `table { vertical-align: top }` (table = `top`, tbody/tr/td = `middle`). tests/setupStyles.test.ts:59 departs only the `table` in `ancestors`, and :79 asserts `expect(attributeDeparture(cell, 'vertical-align', options)).toBe('inherited')`. Lines :87-90 `adoptSheet('table { white-space: nowrap; vertical-align: middle }')` ... `expect(readLonghands(cell).get('vertical-align')).toBe('middle')` pass with or without that rule. In preservation-5b.log the 5 live `inherited` cells (th/td of `table.table.table-sm.align-middle…`) sit under a `tbody` that departs top→middle as `resolved` (Bootstrap's `.table > tbody { vertical-align: inherit }`), so their `tr` parent departed too.
confirmed.defect: The walk returns 'inherited' for a departure on thead/tbody/tfoot, whose UA value is `middle` and not `inherit`. It also returns 'inherited' for a td/th whose tr and section did not depart when only the table did. Chromium 141 cannot produce either state by inheritance, so an unscanned cause on such an element is accepted as 'inherited' instead of refused. The unit proof asserts the impossible state as correct, and its browser-premise assertion uses the value that tbody's UA rule already gives. That assertion cannot fail, which breaks tests.md: 'confirm each assertion would fail for the defect it claims to catch'. Ruling 2d's element list and its 'up to and including the table' go beyond the UA rule the ruling cites, which names only tr, td, and th, and the implementation follows the broader wording.
confirmed.fix: Restrict the departing set to `tr, th, td`, and return 'inherited' only when `element.parentElement` departed in vertical-align. The UA `inherit` reads the parent, and the parent's own departure keeps its own cause. Rewrite the comment to state that rule. In tests/setupStyles.test.ts: (1) put the positive case's departure on the `tr`; (2) add a case where only the `table` departs, which must give 'unattributed'; (3) replace the premise with `table { vertical-align: top }` and assert the cell still reads `middle`; (4) add `tbody { vertical-align: inherit }` and assert the cell then reads `top`. The five live departures keep 'inherited' because each parent `tr` departed. The Orchestrator amends ruling 2d's wording.

I could not refute the finding. The code, Chromium 141's user-agent sheet, a fresh probe, the unit test and the live log all match what the reviewer says.

**The walk is wider than the browser's rule.** The `vertical-align` walk at `tests/setupStyles.ts:622-632` checks `thead`, `tbody` and `tfoot` as well as `tr`, `th` and `td`. It also returns `inherited` when any table-internal ancestor departed, all the way up to the `table`. Chromium 141 (and the HTML Rendering section) give `thead`, `tbody`, `tfoot` and `table > tr` the value `middle`. Only `tr`, `td` and `th` get `inherit`. So by the UA sheet, a departure on the `table` alone never reaches a `tbody` or a cell.

**The unit test pins a state Chromium cannot produce.** `tests/setupStyles.test.ts:59` makes only the `table` depart, and :79 expects `inherited` on the `td`. The premise check at :87-90 cannot fail, because the cell reads `middle` from the `tbody` UA rule with or without `table { vertical-align: middle }`. That breaks the cited tests.md rule, "confirm each assertion would fail for the defect it claims to catch", which exists in scaffold's `tests.md`.

**The defect is reachable.** The scan sets no cause for a rule found in the lifted sheet. It also sets none for a non-exact rule in the recipe's `utilities` layer. Either kind of departure falls through to the walk, which can then accept it as `inherited` instead of refusing it.

**The proposed fix keeps the live results.** In `preservation-5b.log`, all 5 `inherited` cells sit under a `tbody` that departs as `resolved` (Bootstrap's `.table > tbody { vertical-align: inherit }`). Their parent `tr` rows are in the ancestors map, because `ordered` takes in every ancestor of each reader. So a check that only looks at the parent still gives these 5 cells `inherited`.

**The ruling does not excuse it.** The implementation follows ruling 2d word for word, and the finding says so. But the ruling's own premise names only `tr`, `td` and `th`, and ruling 2 requires each correction to state a rule of CSS or of the browser. The wider walk does not state the browser's rule, so the finding's request to amend the ruling stands.

**Minor caveat that does not change the verdict.** The proposed parent-only fix would still wrongly mark a `tr` built directly under a `table` (no `tbody`), because `table > tr { vertical-align: middle }` blocks that inheritance.
